newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aborigines more likely to die in jail - report.
newsitem.headline: Aborigines more likely to die in jail - report.

text.p: The number of Aborigines dying in Australian prisons has continued to rise, with indigenous people 1.26 times more likely to die while in jail than white prisoners, an official report on aboriginal deaths in custody said on Monday.
Between May 1989 and May 1996, 96 Aborigines died in either prison or police custody, said the report by the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Social Justice Commissioner.
Despite a A$400 million (US$324 million) government campaign since 1989 to prevent indigenous deaths in custody, 22 Aborigines died in 1995, the highest number in eight years.
The main cause of death was suicide by hanging, followed by natural causes as a result of the effects of drugs and alcohol.

"There has been a significant decline in the proportion of deaths occuring in police custody and an increase in deaths occuring in prison," said the report, titled Indigenous Deaths in Custody 1989 to 1996.
About two thirds of the deaths occured in prison.
The report said the high death rate reflected the disproportionately high number of Aborigines in custody.
The report found that across the population as a whole, indigenous people were 16.5 times more likely to die in custody than non-indigenous Australians between 1990 and 1995.
Indigenous people were also 17.3 times more likely to be arrested than non-indigenous people, usually for offences such as drunkeness, assault, breaking and entering and car theft.
"Many indigenous people are being placed in custody for trivial offences," the report said.
